text:
Alex M.: Hey team — I opened a PR (#8421) to add a "capacity first-runbook" for Dedicated customers. It combines a Terraform quick example, a Node + Go SDK snippet, and a migration note for the old scale_policy schema. Looking for content + wording review.
Tara D.: on it. quick skim — are we including a sample `scale_policy_v2` YAML, or do we show both old + new for migration clarity?
Alex M.: both. PR currently has: 1) terraform minimal reserved pool snippet, 2) scale_policy_v2 example, 3) small migration table that maps fields from `scale_policy` -> `scale_policy_v2`.
Manny I.: can you paste the terraform block here? want to sanity-check labels/isolation settings.
Alex M.: sure
Alex M.: ```hcl
resource "redwood_dedicated_pool" "example" {
  name      = "prod-pool-01"
  region    = "us-west-2"
  instance_type = "rdi.gpu.p4"
  reserved_capacity = 4
  tenant_labels = ["team:search", "sensitivity:low"]
  isolation = "tenant-isolated"
}
```
Manny I.: looks fine. change `tenant_labels` to key/value map in the snippet? our terraform provider actually supports map shape — might prevent confusion.
Tara D.: good catch. also we should explain isolation modes briefly: `tenant-isolated`, `best-effort`, and `reserved`. small callout about eviction vs preemption wording — product wants "eviction" used only for infra-driven preemption; SLA language should say "may be evicted under overload" -> sounds alarm-y. maybe soften to "may be preempted under capacity constraints".
Liam S.: +1 on softer wording. ops/legal reviewed the SLA blurb last week — prefer "capacity-dependent eviction may occur for best-effort deployments". we should put an inline link to the SLA page.
Alex M.: I'll update phrasing. Tara can you own the migration table? make it clear which fields are required in v2 and which are deprecated.
Tara D.: taking it. I'll add a small example that shows how to translate `min_instances` -> `min_replicas`, `burst_policy` -> `scale_windows`. also adding a one-liner about backward-compat behavior in the runtime.
Manny I.: for the SDK snippets: I added a tiny Node example but missing error-handling for quota responses. Could we include a `try/catch` with suggested fallback to `fallback_model` route? simple snippet:
Manny I.: ```js
try {
  const res = await client.dedicated.createPool({ /*...*/ });
} catch (err) {
  if (err.code === 'QUOTA_EXCEEDED') {
    // fallback: route to hosted api
  }
}
```
Tara D.: perfect. please also include an example of `autoscale` YAML with comments for `cooldown_seconds` and `stabilization_window` — those confuse users.
Alex M.: added one in the PR but it's sparse. here's the current snippet:
Alex M.: ```yaml
scale_policy_v2:
  name: search-autoscale
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 20
  metrics:
    - type: rps
      target: 500
  cooldown_seconds: 120
  stabilization_window: 300
```
Liam S.: can we annotate that `stabilization_window` is recommended to be >= `cooldown_seconds` for smoother rollouts? add a note about canary ramp if customers want gradual additions.
Tara D.: will add inline note. Also found one broken link in the handbook section pointing to the old `scale_policy` doc — will update to the new migration anchor. docs-bot, can you create a link check for the PR branch?
docs-bot: linkcheck job queued for branch alex/8421-runbook — results should appear as a check on the PR in ~5 minutes.
Alex M.: sweet. final asks before I request review: - confirm terraform map change, - migration table by Tara, - SLA wording tweak (Liam/Manny sign-off), - add autoscale comment edits.
Manny I.: terraform map change looks good to me. SLA wording: "capacity-dependent preemption may occur for best-effort deployments" gets my sign-off.
Liam S.: sign-off as well, thanks. Tara taking migration + YAML notes.
Tara D.: done. I'm pushing an update with the map snippet, migration table, and annotated YAML. will request review from @docs-team and @infra after CI/linkcheck.
Alex M.: thanks y'all — will wait for CI then request reviews. :thumbsup:
